history.summary: Hindu temple housed in the RCS Building, PWD Tlang, Babutlang, Upper Bazar, Zarkawt, Aizawl 796001 (geocoded address corroborated by two independent place datasets). It serves Aizawl's small Hindu minority (largely Gorkha and other non-Mizo communities) in a Christian-majority state. Rated ~4.5-4.9 by 30-40 online reviewers. No published source gives a founding date, builder, or architectural description — identity of the presiding deity is inferred from the name only. No reliable photograph of this temple was found after genuine searching, so media is left empty.

name: Shakti Mandir
town_description: Aizawl is the capital of Mizoram, a hill city built on steep ridges at around 1,130 m elevation in the state's northern hills. Overwhelmingly Christian (Mizo) in population, it is the political, commercial and cultural centre of the state, with a small Hindu minority of Gorkha, Bihari and other non-Mizo communities who maintain the city's handful of temples.

travel.airport: Lengpui Airport, ~35 km northwest of Aizawl (verify).
travel.railway: Nearest railhead Bairabi, ~110 km (verify); Sairang line under construction (verify).
travel.road: Aizawl is connected to Silchar (~180 km) and Guwahati (~450 km) by NH-6; city taxis/auto-rickshaws within town (verify).
